sentence_stem: If only I had studied harder,
correct_completion: I would have passed the exam.
full_sentence: If only I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
acceptable_variants: I might have passed the exam.
I could have passed the exam.

options.why_wrong: This states a past fact. 'If only' expresses an unreal past situation, so the result must be imagined, not real.
This is a future plan. A regret about the past needs a result that did not happen in the past.

options.text: I would have passed the exam.

options.why_wrong: This is a past fact that the speaker did not do, so it does not complete the unreal result that 'if only' introduces.

grammar_focus: Third conditional with 'if only' for past regrets
explanation: 'If only' plus the past perfect expresses a regret about the past. The main clause uses 'would have' plus the past participle to show the result that did not happen.
translation: Se eu tivesse estudado mais, eu teria passado no exame.
